q: Does the static-MPF quadratic error-order improvement (p to p+2) hold for time-dependent Hamiltonians H(t), where the base Trotter S_2 itself acquires additional error terms from the time ordering (Dyson / Magnus corrections)?
basis: The paper's Section V numerics and Theorem 1 are stated for time-independent H. Dynamic MPF (Section VI) allows time-dependent coefficients but the underlying commutator-scaling proof for time-dependent H is not spelled out. Our replication tested only static H.
next_steps: Implement a time-dependent test problem (e.g., driven transverse-field Ising with h_x(t) = h0 + A sin(omega t)) at n=4-6 qubits. Compute exact reference via a fine Runge-Kutta or Magnus-4 propagator. Apply the same MPF with k = lambda*(4,13,17) and c = (0.016088, -1.794934, 2.778846) using a Magnus-based S_2. Fit slope of MPF error vs lambda; compare to -4 target. Sweep drive frequency omega across adiabatic and non-adiabatic regimes.

q: How does the static MPF compare to (and possibly compose with) qubitization / LCU-based simulation on the same Hamiltonian in a matched-query-complexity comparison?
basis: Qubitization achieves optimal query complexity O(t + log(1/eps)) but has larger per-query overhead and ancilla count. The MPF sits in the product-formula family with far lower ancilla cost. A head-to-head Pareto frontier (queries vs error vs ancilla) on the same Childs-Maslov Heisenberg chain was not in the paper.
next_steps: Implement qubitization via Qiskit's built-in block-encoding utilities for the Childs-Maslov H at n=4-8. Report (T-count, ancilla count, achieved error) for qubitization at several precision targets. Overlay MPF (T-count, 0 ancilla, achieved error) curves. Identify crossover t and eps where each method wins. Also test MPF as a stand-alone block-encoding building block inside LCU (each rho_k as an LCU term).

q: Does the MPF-with-fixed-coefficients advantage persist for realistic chemistry (electronic-structure) and lattice-gauge Hamiltonians whose commutator structure differs sharply from the disordered Heisenberg chain benchmark?
basis: The paper's numerics only cover Childs-Maslov Heisenberg. Chemistry Hamiltonians (H2, LiH, N2 in a moderate basis) have all-to-all fermionic 2-body terms and highly non-uniform commutator norms; lattice Schwinger / Z2 gauge theories have gauge-constraint structure. The coefficient set (0.016088, -1.794934, 2.778846) may or may not be near-optimal for those settings.
next_steps: For chemistry: build the Jordan-Wigner-mapped H2 / LiH Hamiltonians (n=4, 12 qubits) from PySCF; run the same MPF and fit lambda-slope. For lattice: build the 1+1D Schwinger model at 4-6 sites and repeat. Report whether the -4 slope holds, and whether re-optimizing (k_i, c_i) per Hamiltonian yields further improvement.

q: How robust is the static MPF (with the paper's fixed c coefficients) to realistic 2-qubit gate noise (coherent + incoherent), and where is the crossover error rate at which noise dominates the Trotter error the MPF is designed to cancel?
basis: The paper introduces Minimax MPF (Section VII) specifically to address noise but its own numerics for that section were not exercised in our replication. Under gate noise the c_i become effective mixing coefficients on noisy density matrices; the cancellation that gives O(1/lambda^4) may fail.
next_steps: Use Qiskit AerSimulator with a depolarizing noise model at 2-qubit rates in {1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2}. Run the same k = lambda*(4,13,17) MPF at n=4, t=1, lambda in {1..4}. Compare to noiseless MPF and to noisy single Trotter at matched k_max. Identify the lambda at which increasing lambda no longer helps because noise depth dominates. Compare against a re-optimized Minimax MPF from Section VII.

q: On a sample-cost (total shot count) Pareto frontier, does the static MPF still beat standard Trotter after amortizing the constant-factor circuit-repetition overhead and the shot-noise cost of estimating multiple rho_{k_i} in the linear combination?
basis: The paper's cost accounting is in circuit depth / gate count at fixed error. Real experiments pay in shots: each rho_{k_i} must be sampled to sufficient precision so that sum c_i * rho_{k_i} has controlled shot variance. Large |c_2| = 1.79 and |c_3| = 2.78 amplify shot noise relative to a single-circuit Trotter estimate.
next_steps: Compute achievable observable estimation error <O> for a low-locality observable (e.g., Z_0 Z_1) under both approaches at matched total shot budget N in {1e4, 1e5, 1e6}. Derive analytic variance formula for the MPF estimator using c_i^2 sum. Plot (shot budget vs observable error) for MPF vs Trotter at matched k_max. Identify the shot-budget regime where MPF wins. Cross-check against Minimax-MPF coefficients designed to minimize the sample-cost objective.
